title: Follow along: one list of leads, and the follow-up you should not send
goal: Sort ten leads by next step date, see who went quiet, let AI draft three follow-ups, catch the two that should not go out, and leave with a list where every open lead has a next step and a date.
you_need: This demo, open in a browser
An AI chat you are signed in to (Claude or ChatGPT)
Optional: your own lead list, in Google Sheets or as a CRM export

steps.do: Open the demo (double-click Launch) and click Week 6.
steps.see: The lead list: 10 leads, 6 gone quiet, with Today is set to November 11.
steps.tip: Every name here is made up. Your real CRM stays closed.

steps.do: Click the Name header in the table, then click the Next step date header. Count the amber rows.
steps.see: By name it is a phone book. By date it is a to-do list: four amber rows with a date gone by at the top, two with no date at the bottom.
steps.tip: The two with no date worry me more. Nothing will ever remind anyone.

steps.do: Go to step 2. Check that Greg, Victor and Angela are ticked, then read the rules in the prompt out loud.
steps.see: Today is November 11, 2026. Never invent a price or a date. Under 80 words. Sound like a person. Ask one question.
steps.tip: The email and phone columns are not in what gets copied. The AI does not need them to write a draft.

steps.do: Press Copy the prompt and the leads. Paste into your AI chat and send. Copy its whole answer.
steps.see: A list of the quiet leads, then three drafts that each start with DRAFT FOR and a name.
steps.tip: No AI chat handy? In step 3, press No AI handy? Load the sample answer.

steps.do: Paste the answer into step 3, Bring the drafts back, and press Use this answer.
steps.see: Step 4 fills with cards: each draft sits under that lead's notes.
steps.tip: If no cards appear, ask the AI to start each draft with DRAFT FOR and the lead's name.

steps.do: Which one is wrong? Read Victor's notes, then Angela's. Press Do not send on every draft you would hold back.
steps.see: The reason appears under the draft. With the sample answer: Victor already said no, and Angela's draft names a day that is not in her notes.
steps.tip: Your own AI's drafts will differ. React to what is there. Greg's is the one to send.

steps.do: On Victor's card press Close this lead as Lost. On Greg's card press Mark as sent, type the next step, pick a date and press Save the next step.
steps.see: Victor's card says a no is a good outcome. Greg's card says he has left the quiet list. The title of step 1 now says 4 gone quiet.
steps.tip: No card for Victor? Your AI read his notes well. Set his stage to Lost in step 5 instead.

steps.do: Scroll to Where leads come from and read the bars. Then press Copy for Google Sheets or Excel and paste into a blank sheet.
steps.see: Website form brought four of the ten leads. Your sheet has every column, with the changes you just made.
steps.tip: Source is the one column that pays for itself.

steps.see: A new number on your one screen: leads gone quiet.
steps.tip: Next Wednesday: where all of this data should live, and one screen to see it.

real_life: Tonight: in step 1 open Use my own leads, paste the rows from your own sheet or CRM export with the header row first, and press Use these leads.
In step 5, give every open lead a next step and a date. Then send the oldest follow-up yourself. The AI drafts it. You read it and press send.
Put a 10-minute pipeline check on your calendar for every working day: open the list, sort by date, do what is due.
if_it_breaks: The AI is slow or down: press No AI handy? Load the sample answer and keep going. The lesson is the checking, not the typing.
No draft cards after pasting: each draft has to start with a line that says DRAFT FOR and the lead's name. Ask the AI to redo it in that shape.
The quiet count looks wrong: check the date next to Today is, at the top of step 1. Start over with the sample data puts everything back.
